beats.say: Hello! I am your security helper. Today you will learn to spot scams that come by phone.
The screen shows the bank's name, but a caller's name and number are easy to fake.
Scammers rush you: your card is blocked, money is leaving. Fear and haste are their main weapons.

checkpoint.prompt: The caller asks for your text message code. What do you do?

options.label: I read out the code
options.feedback: This code can open your account or approve a payment. A bank never asks for it.

options.label: I hang up and call the bank myself
options.feedback: Correct. This check completely breaks the scammer's plan.

beats.say: Golden rule: hang up and call the official number yourself, from your card or the official website.

scenes.title: A call from the bank
scenes.intro: The screen shows your bank's name. Listen to the caller and choose your answer at each step.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answering is not dangerous. What matters is what you say.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: That works too. If worried, call the number on the back of your card yourself.

steps.say: Hello, this is Fuad Mammadov from SahilBank security. Someone is trying to take 1,200 manat from your card right now.
steps.spoken: Hello, <breath> this is Fuad Mammadov from SahilBank security. Someone is trying to, uh, take 1,200 manat from your card right now.

actions.label: I give the last card digits
actions.feedback: Your bank already knows you and does not need this. Every detail makes the scammer more convincing.

actions.label: I share no card details by phone
actions.feedback: Right. Never give card details on an incoming call; the name and number can be faked.

steps.say: You have five minutes to stop it. Read me the code that just came to your phone, and tell no one.
steps.spoken: You have five minutes to stop it. <breath> Read me the code that just came to your phone, and tell no one.

actions.label: I read out the code
actions.feedback: The SMS code approves a payment. Reading it out means you send the money yourself.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Right. No bank asks for an SMS code by phone.

steps.say: Then move your money to a safe account to protect it. I am sending the details by SMS now.
steps.spoken: Then, uh, move your money to a safe account to protect it. <breath> I am sending the details by SMS now.

actions.label: I move the money to the safe account
actions.feedback: There is no safe account: it belongs to the scammer. A bank never asks you to move money.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Great decision. Asking you to move money is the scam's final step.

steps.label: The call has ended. What do you do now?

actions.label: Call the number on the card
actions.feedback: Right. Dial the official number yourself, ideally from another phone, so the line cannot stay open.

actions.label: Call back the incoming number
actions.feedback: The number can be faked. Take the number from your card or the bank's official website.

question.prompt: The screen shows the bank's official number. Is the call real?

options.label: Yes, if the number is right, the call is real
options.feedback: A number can be faked. The number on the screen is not proof.

options.label: I cannot tell, so I call back myself
options.feedback: Correct. Dial the official number yourself, ideally from another phone, so the scammer cannot keep the line open.

options.label: I ask for their name, that is enough
options.feedback: A scammer can give any name. A name is not a check.

scenes.explain: A caller's name and number can be fake. The safest way is to hang up and call the official number yourself.

body.text: This is the police. A loan was opened in your name. Move your money to a safe account now.

cards.explain: The police never ask you to move money to a safe account. This is a well known scam.

body.text: We saw a suspicious payment on your card. Do not tell us anything, call the number on the back of your card.

cards.explain: It asks for nothing and sends you to the official number. Call the number on your card to check.

body.text: Your mailbox has a virus. Tell me your password and I will clean it remotely.

cards.explain: Technical support does not need your password. Never tell it to anyone.

body.text: I am calling about the request you opened yesterday. We will update your computer tomorrow, you do not need to do anything.

cards.explain: You opened the request yourself and nothing is asked of you. This is a normal work call.

body.text: To protect your account, install this app so I can see your screen.

cards.explain: A remote control app hands them your whole phone. A bank never asks for this.

nodes.text: Hello, this is Elvin from technical support. Your account is being blocked, we need to confirm your password now.
nodes.speaker: Caller
nodes.spoken: Hello, this is Elvin from technical support. <breath> Your account is being blocked, we need to confirm your password now.

choices.label: I tell my password
choices.feedback: Someone else now has your password. Change it at once and report it to support on the official number.

choices.label: I ask who they are
choices.feedback: A good start, but do not fully trust the answer.

choices.label: I hang up and call support myself
choices.feedback: Excellent. Real technical support never asks for your password.

nodes.text: I am Elvin Hasanov, third floor. Hurry, the account will be deleted in five minutes. At least install this program.
nodes.speaker: Caller
nodes.spoken: I am Elvin Hasanov, third floor. Hurry, uh, the account will be deleted in five minutes. At least install this program.

choices.label: I install the program
choices.feedback: With a remote control program, he can see and control your computer.

choices.label: I say I will call back myself
choices.feedback: The right call. Rushing is a warning sign, and calling back is the best check.

nodes.text: An unknown program opens and the cursor moves on its own.

choices.label: I disconnect and call support
choices.feedback: The right reaction. Reporting fast limits the damage.

choices.label: I feel embarrassed and tell no one
choices.feedback: Silence gives the attacker time. Reporting is nothing to be ashamed of, it protects everyone.

points: A caller's name and number can be fake
Never tell anyone a code, PIN or password
Hang up and call the official number yourself
